Finally, it is atheological [ἀθεόλογος], because it rests on no axiom drawn from holy Scripture; it is also easily refuted [εὔλυτος], because its minor premise exposes ignorance [ἀγνοίαν ἐλέγχει] and contains a petition of the principle [petitionem principii].

units.la: CAPVT VIII.
units.tr: CHAPTER VIII.

units.la: RTVRVS libro tertio à cap. II. visque ad 19. aduersus 8. cap. Analysis super. agit de Antiquitate, quam statuit tertiam Ecclesiæ notam: Adami tempore, inquit, Ecclesia fuit antiqua non affirmatiue, vt philosophi loquuntur, sed negatiue, quoniam nulla fuit in terris antiquior. In die autem Pentecostes etiam affirmatiue, quia omnes alios hominum coetus temporis diuturnitate superauit. Si id est verius quod prius & antiquius. Ergo Antiquitas est veritatis & Ecclesiæ vera nota. Affirmatio naturâ negationem præcedit: Itaque nemo sic loquutus est philosophus vt iste loquitur. Affirmatiue semper fuit Ecccclesia Christi: perperam igitur hic affirmat negatiue, vt nota illa sua stabiliat. Conferenda est istius respōsio cū iis quæ dicta sunt in Analysi superiore, vt appareat quàm sit item inepta distinctio: cuius est etiā Connexū ridiculū. Nā debuit colligere. Ergo Antiquius est veritatis: vel Antiquitas est in veritate respectu certorū temporū. Veritas autē est prima & antiquissima. Quòd si tibi idem est Antiquū & verū: pernegamus Ecclesiā veterā esse Antiquā & errores pōrificios licet antiquos, negamus tamē esse antiquissimos. Nā antiquitas arcessenda est ab ipso Christo & Apostolis, qui sunt nobis ϖαλαιοί: doctrinā nimirū diuinā ita tuimus nobis fuisse in verbo Dei scripto patefacta: quod antiquius est quàm sint istæ pōtificię & monachales Traditiones. Hæc igitur est præclara scil. Assertoris istius ratiocinatio. Ecclesia Rom. est vera Ecclesia quia est antiqua: & antiqua quia est vera. At nos ipsam Antiquitatem tibi eripimus & Ecclesiæ Reformatæ iure eam tribuimus. Nam veritas est proprie antiqua: errores verò, illius respectu, sunt Noui. Veritatis regula prior, inquit Tertullianus. Samosatenus fuit Ario prior & antiquior: sed non propterea fuit purior aut melior. Sic sunt multi doctores praui antiqui. Nos autē non nouā doctrinā aut nouā Ecclesiā profitemur. Nā aliud est ordiri Ecclesiā, aliud errores reiicere vt reformetur Ecclesia. Nec Romanā Ecclesiā dicimus esse falsam & defe-rendā, ea ratione quòd sit antiqua: vt falsò nobis Arturus tribuit: sed ex eò, quòd veritatis capu atque origine reliquerit: vnde natas omnes hærehæresesaffirmat Augustinus. Ecclesiæ vero Reformatę Apostolicâ tum doctrinâ tum Ecclesiam à pôrificiis quoad cius fieri potuit, consepultâ excitant. Ita liberatio Ecclesiæ apud Ezech. capite 37. cum resurrectione comparatur. Nam Deo vlciscente hominū ingratitudinem (qui vt ait Ioânes tenebras dilexerūt pro luce) euenit vt effusis Papismi tenebris nec Ecclesia nec Scriptura coruscaret. Vos vos Pōtificij, vos monachi, candelabrū e ertiftis, quantū in vobis fuit. Vos lucernā sub modio posuistis: lucernam plane extincturi, nisi Deus mirada ratione illā rursus excitasset, fuit Ecclesia ab Apostolis super monte posita: postea fuit detur-bata, manuitque in ruderibus magnâ Dei providentia conseruata. Nō enim ex eo quòd Ecclesia Christi nunquam sit in terris interitura, colligendū est eā semper omnibus esse conspicua. Nū quotquot non sunt expositi omniū oculis, interierunt? Nec præstātia Ecclesiæ in eo sita est, quòd ab omnibus vel à pluribus conspiciatur. Professio exterior, templū, sacri ritus in vetere Ecclesia sæpe fuisse interrupta ex sacra historia liquet, Sacerdotes Iudaici, Pharisæi Sadducæi volitabant, quū discipuli propter illorū metu inclusi delitescebant. Prophetæ describūt quidè Ecclesiæ Christianæ amplitudinē, quod & impletū fuit Apostolorū tempore Col.1. Apostasiā verò prædictā ab Apostolis Pōtifices Romani impleuerunt. Porrò si facit Ecclesiam Diffusio & Antiquitas: Iudæorū synagoga esset Ecclesia. Ex veritate igitur nō ex diffusione, externo splendore, & ementita Antiquitate dignoscenda est Ecclesia. Itaque Iudæi & monachi pontificij quia veritatem non seruât, nó sunt vera Ecclesia. Et perperam ita cóclu- dunt isti:Non vidimus, non vidistis. Ergo Ec- clesia vera non delituit.Et iste Monachus non credit aliquid delitescere, nisi illud videat. Eò ipso quod probamus apud Pontificios veram Ecclesiâ non fuisse:simul probamus veram Ec- clesiam delituisse, quum tyrannis pontificia locum obtineret. Sic quû Israëlitæ idemtidem Iudicum temporibus ad idololatriâ recidêrét, dico tû Ecclesiam delituisse. Itê, quû Israëlitæ essent sine lege & doctore,2.Chron.15.Perperâ statuit etiâ Allertor nulla esse vnqua alia ratione conseruanda Ecclesiæ præter Publicû ordine & præ ter Martyriû.Nâ Enstascs in superiore Analysi & aduersus Turrianû allatæ,sunt locupletissi- mæ: quibus illud euertitur pronunciatum sine testimonio produćtû.Nâ Deus nec externo pu blico ordini nec perpetuo martyrio Ecclesiâ suâ alligauit : quòd ex Ezech.c.37.7.8.& 9.co- probari,demonstratu fuit in sup. Analysi. Vbi sit comparatio cum terebyntho & quercu qu̧ glandes amiserit,vt docet Hieronymus(nec Al- sertor,vim Hebraicæ linguæ nó percipiés, ca- uilletur Sadeelem sententiâ illius loci, nó ipsa verba exprimere)hàc tamê emortuâ propterea non dicemus,quandiu succus vitalis in radice hęrebit.Locus verò quê allertor ex Esaiæ cap. 54.obiicit:Lætare sterilis,quæ non paris,&c.im- pleta est nó téporibus Papismi, sed Apost.Et ad Gal.4.docetur,Esaiam agere de Electis siue de filiis secundû promissione. Imò ex illo loco popotius colligitur: Ecclesiam, quae ad tepus desferta fuit & sterilis, maxima prolem habitura. Etenim Ecclesia Dei delitescés in mediis tenebris emersit, nó ex Oceano (vt assertor mete captus illudens ait) sed ex erroribus & corruptelis: tum olim Pharisaicis & Iudaicis, tum etiam nouissimis tèporib. quum Deus lucé Euägelij quasi sopita accédit, monachalib. & Pótificiis.
units.tr: Returning in the third book, from chapter 2 to chapter 19, against chapter 8 of the earlier Analysis, he treats of Antiquity, which he has set up as the third mark of the Church. "In the time of Adam," he says, "the Church was ancient not affirmatively, as the philosophers put it, but negatively, since there was none older on earth. On the day of Pentecost, however, it was ancient also affirmatively, because it surpassed all other assemblies of men in the length of its duration. If that is truer which is prior and more ancient, then antiquity is the mark of truth and a true mark of the Church." Affirmation comes before negation in nature, so no philosopher has ever spoken as he does. The Church of Christ has always been ancient affirmatively; he therefore wrongly affirms it negatively in order to establish his mark. My answer to him should be set beside what was said in the earlier Analysis, so that it becomes clear how absurd that distinction is, and his connection is ridiculous as well. For he ought to have concluded: "Therefore the older is the true, or antiquity is found in truth with respect to certain times." But truth is first and most ancient. And if for you the ancient and the true are the same thing, then we flatly deny that the old Roman church is the ancient Church. Though the Papist errors are old, we deny that they are the most ancient, for antiquity must be traced back to Christ himself and the Apostles, who are for us "the ancients." Indeed, that divine doctrine was revealed to us in the written Word of God, and it is older than these papal and monastic traditions. This, then, is the splendid reasoning of that assertor: the Roman Church is the true Church because it is ancient, and it is ancient because it is true. But we snatch antiquity itself away from you and grant it by right to the Reformed Church. For truth is properly ancient, while errors, in comparison with it, are new. "The rule of truth comes first," says Tertullian. Paul of Samosata was earlier and older than Arius, but for that reason he was not purer or better. Many depraved teachers have been ancient in this way. We, however, do not profess a new doctrine or a new Church. It is one thing to found a Church, and another to reject errors so that a Church may be reformed. Nor do we say that the Roman Church is false and to be abandoned on the ground that it is ancient, as Arturus wrongly attributes to us. We say it is false because it has abandoned the head and origin of truth, from which, Augustine affirms, all heresies were born. The Reformed Church, on the other hand, revives the Church, which had been buried together with apostolic doctrine, and frees it from the Papists as far as that was possible. So the deliverance of the Church is compared with a resurrection in Ezekiel 37. For God, avenging men's ingratitude (who, as John says, loved darkness rather than light), it came about that, with the darkness of Papism poured out, neither the Church nor Scripture shone. You, you Papists, you monks, have overturned the candlestick as far as lay in you. You have put the lamp under a bushel, and you would have quite extinguished it, had God not raised it up again by a wonderful plan. The Church was set by the Apostles upon a mountain; afterwards it was thrown into confusion, and it remained preserved amid the ruins by the great providence of God. For it does not follow from the fact that the Church of Christ will never perish on earth that it is always visible to everyone. Have all who are not exposed to everyone's eyes perished? Nor does the excellence of the Church lie in its being seen by all or by most. That the outward profession, the temple, and the sacred rites were often interrupted in the old Church is clear from sacred history: Jewish priests, Pharisees and Sadducees were flitting about, while the disciples, shut in for fear of them, lay hidden. The prophets indeed describe the breadth of the Christian Church, and this was fulfilled in the time of the Apostles (Col. 1). But the Roman pontiffs have fulfilled the apostasy that the Apostles foretold. Moreover, if diffusion and antiquity made the Church, the synagogue of the Jews would be the Church. The Church is therefore to be recognised by truth, not by diffusion, outward splendour, or pretended antiquity. Thus the Jews and the Papist monks, because they do not keep the truth, are not the true Church. And these men conclude wrongly: "We have not seen it, you have not seen it; therefore the true Church has not lain hidden." And this monk does not believe that anything lies hidden unless he sees it. By the very fact that we prove that the true Church did not exist among the Papists, we also prove that the true Church lay hidden while the papal tyranny held the place. So too, when the Israelites, in the times of the Judges, fell back again into idolatry, I say that the Church lay hidden. So too, when the Israelites were without law and teacher (2 Chron. 15). The assertor also wrongly lays down that the Church was never to be preserved by any means other than public order and martyrdom. For the arguments brought forward in the earlier Analysis and against Turrianus are most abundant, and by them that pronouncement, made without any witness produced, is overturned. For God bound his Church neither to an outward public order nor to continual martyrdom, as was demonstrated in the earlier Analysis from Ezekiel 37:7–9. Where there is a comparison with a terebinth and an oak that has lost its acorns, as Jerome teaches (and let the assertor, not grasping the force of the Hebrew language, not carp that Sadeel expresses the sense of that passage rather than the words themselves), we still will not call it dead on that account, as long as the vital sap remains in the root. The passage that the assertor brings against us from Isaiah 54, "Rejoice, barren woman, who does not bear," was fulfilled not in the times of Papism but in those of the Apostles. And Galatians 4 teaches that Isaiah is speaking of the elect, or of the children according to promise. Indeed, it is rather from that passage that one infers this: the Church, which for a time was deserted and barren, was to have a very great offspring. For the Church of God, lying hidden amid the darkness, emerged not from the Ocean (as the assertor, out of his wits, mocks and says) but from errors and corruptions: formerly Pharisaic and Jewish, and also in the latest times, when God stirs up the light of the Gospel as though it had been lulled to sleep, monastic and Papist ones.

units.la: Ex iis quę diximus corruunt ea quae assertor subiicit, inquiens: Si illa Ecclesia antiqua est, quae columna est & firmamentū veritatis, vestra profeßio non est antiqua, quae hanc veritate non agnoscit: & Ecclesia vera, in doctrina errare posse & per mille annos errasse fideiter affirmat. Regerat hoc argumentum Sadeel. Certè nullo negotio totum istud Cónexū euertitur, ex eo quòd tantū adhibeas petitione principij. Quis enim tibi dat Ecclesiam pontificiā vestra cĭse Antiquā & verā?imò cótra docemus illā esse falsam & nouā: ac proinde nó esse columnā & firmamentū veritatis.
units.tr: From what we have said, those things that the opponent adds collapse, saying: If that Church is ancient which is the pillar and ground of truth, your profession is not ancient, since it does not acknowledge this truth; and it firmly asserts that the true Church can err in doctrine and has erred for a thousand years. Let Sadeel answer this argument. Certainly this whole line of reasoning is overturned without any trouble, from the fact that you use nothing but begging the question. For who grants you that your Papist Church is ancient and true? On the contrary, we teach that it is false and new, and therefore is not the pillar and ground of truth.

units.la: Nā satis à nobis audiuisti quaenā sit nobis Ecclesia antiqua & vera: ea nimirū quae prisćam veramque retinet doctrinam: Atqui vestra Ecclesia hanc doctrinā non retinet, ergo non est antiqua. Recte igitur sic in te retorqueatur argumentū tuū. Illi autē antiquā habent doctrinam & verā qui ab Apostolorū tèporib. vbiuis locorū & gentiū, sacrae Scripturae adhærēt doctrinaeqj in illa patefactae. Illa vera est antiquitas quę est columna & firmamentū veritatis.
units.tr: For you have heard from us often enough what, for us, is the ancient and true Church: namely, the one that keeps the original and true doctrine. But your Church does not keep this doctrine; therefore it is not ancient. Your argument, then, may rightly be turned back upon you in this way: those have an ancient and true doctrine who, from the times of the Apostles, in every place and among every people, cling to Holy Scripture and to the doctrine revealed in it. That is the true antiquity which is the pillar and ground of truth.

units.la: Ita pij veteres Christiani (quos per ludibrium quū obiectas nó fuisse Lutheranos aut Calvinianos, nō tamē probas fuisse Iesuitas aut Pōtificios)Christiani,inquam,vt & nos fumus,ex facrisScripturis perperá ab hereticis vsurpatis, hæresçs & falsam doctrinâ refellebat: idque nó est in Opertis scripturis immorari, quæ nó sunt pallio impietatis, vt tu blasphemè & impiè audus es dicere, impudenter impietate tuâ Nazianzeno adscribens, qui potiùs monebat illos in cœno immorari & luto adhærescere qui non contendunt ad purissimu scripturarū diuinarum fontem: quas alibi dicit,illos solos posse cernere, quibus mens purgata est: sed tu amens sacræ Scripturæ contemptor & vellicator pluris facis Episcoporum auctoritatem & quorundam monachorum commenta. Atqui Deus hanc vlciscetur impietatem.
units.tr: So the godly ancient Christians (whom, mockingly, you object were not Lutherans or Calvinists, yet you do not prove that they were Jesuits or Papists), Christians, I say, as we are, refuted heresies and false doctrine from the sacred Scriptures, which heretics had wrongly seized upon; and this is not to linger among the apocryphal writings, which are not a cloak for impiety, as you have blasphemously and impiously dared to say, shamelessly ascribing your own impiety to Nazianzen, who rather warned those who do not hasten to the purest fountain of the divine Scriptures to linger in mud and cling to the slime. Elsewhere he says that only those can perceive these things whose mind has been cleansed. But you, a madman who despises and carps at Holy Scripture, set greater store by the authority of bishops and the inventions of certain monks. Yet God will avenge this impiety.

units.la: Quid præterea habet bonus ille quod exprobret: Vestri, inquit, è Catechismis suis & è Symbolo vocabulum Catholicæ eradunt. Vnde tibi illa incessit Religio verborum scrupulosa assertori, vt non patiaris, nos vocabulo vernaculo Græcum vocabulū exprimere, & iis quæ in S. Scriptura extant adhærescere? Nā voces peregrino idiomate rudioribus propositæ nec fideliter expositæ admiratione nó ædificatione afferūt. Ideo fideles doctores iis abstinent. Nos igitur Vniuersale Ecclesiam dicimus. Necid ingratū esse debet Pontificiis Latinā linguam & Ecclesiam solā extollētibus, & qui Græcas habent exosas Ecclesias vnde tamen Catholicæ vocabulū manauit, quòd à nostris cōmodè explicatur: cuius etiam est explanatio copiosa adu. Turr. loco 1. Scrip. Et ibi ad Repet. eiusdē Soph. & in summa adu. Mon. Burd. art. 60.
units.tr: What else has that good man to reproach us with? "Yours," he says, "erase the word Catholic [καθολικὴ] from their Catechisms and from the Creed." Where did such a scrupulous regard for words come upon you, as a champion of this cause, that you will not allow us to render a Greek word by a native word and to keep to what is found in Holy Scripture? For words set before untutored readers in a foreign idiom, if not faithfully explained, bring wonder rather than edification. Therefore faithful teachers abstain from them. So we say the universal Church. Nor ought it to be thought ungrateful of us, since the Papists extol the Latin language and the Church alone, and hold the Greek churches in hatred, that the word Catholic nonetheless came from them, and our people explain it fittingly. A full explanation of this is given against Turrianus, in the first locus of Scripture, and there again in the reply to the same Sophist, and in summary against the Burdegalensian Monitory, article 60.

units.la: CAPUT IX.
units.tr: CHAPTER IX.

units.la: ASsertor lib. 3. cap. 19. vsque ad 24. agit de Quarta Ecclesiae sua nota: nepe quod sit Apostolica in succession Episcoporum vt impugnet caput nonu Analysis thefeum Arturi: qui nunc sic loquitur. Non solum haereticis Successio doctrina: sed etiam Episcoporum obiecta fuit ab Iren. Tertull. Cypriano, &c. visibilis successio quae nunquam perturbabitur. Sadeel Doctorum successionem in genere dicit. Episcopi vero & Pontifex rectè sua munia obire costat. Nam satis est bene praesse. Qui bene praesunt, inquit Apost. 1. Tim. 5. Hinc laudes Episcoporum Romanorum profert, &c.
units.tr: The Assertor, in book 3, chapters 19 to 24, treats of the fourth mark of his Church, namely that it is apostolic in the succession of bishops, in order to attack chapter nine of Arturus's Analysis of the Theses, where he now speaks thus: The doctrine of succession was objected not only to heretics but also to bishops by Irenaeus, Tertullian, Cyprian, etc.: a visible succession which will never be disturbed. Sadeel speaks of a succession of teachers in general. But that bishops and the Pope discharge their duties rightly is plain, for it is enough that they preside well. Those who preside well, says the Apostle in 1 Tim. 5. Hence he brings forward the praises of the Roman bishops, etc.

units.la: De hac Successione in Episcopis & personis sita quam Pontificij iactat fusè in libro de legit. pastorum vocatione: & aduersus monachos Burdegal. Art. 51 61. Aduersus Turrianum in Indice Art. 20. & ad eius Sophismata loco Script. 9. & 10. integris. & ad Repet. eius Soph. loco 1. Art. 29. 30. 31. 32. 33. 46. 47. & loco 9. art. 1. 6. 7. Et loco 10. toto & loco 3. Art. 4. 5. & loco 4. Art. 9. Ex quibus petenda est refutatio eorum quae hic Arturus repetit, qui initio capitis 10. lib. 3. videtur dissimulare se scripta Sadeelis aduersus Turrianum de hoc argumento vidisse, alibi tamen dixerat Turrianum innocentissimum à Sadeele vexari.Docuit autem Sadeel illis in locis & in superiori Analysi:Illis Veteribus facile fuisse ex vtraque Successione haereticos refellere: quum doctrinæ veritas continua successione propagabatur: sic illi vtramque successionem coniungebant. Sed vos qui à veritate doctrinæ & ab ipsa legitima vocatione excidistis, Personalé successionem,successioni doctrinę opponitis,plurisque facitis visibilem personarum successionē quàm Apostolicæ doctrinæ continuationem & perseuerantiam. At ipsi Veteres testantur in successione personarum nihil esse momenti, si à continuatione & perseuerantia doctrinæ diuellatur. Nam veritas sine personali successione, & personalis successio sine veritate potest esse. Hoc in Iudaica Ecclesia comprobatur. Erat etiam successio Episcoporum in Oriente grassente Arianismo:sed non veritatis. Nonne est in Græcia personalis Episcoporum successio? cur igitur à Pontificiis Romanis excidisse dicuntur nisi quòd veram doctrinam reliquerint?Ergo arcessennda est successio ab Apostolica doctrina: Vnde enim veritas?nónne ab Apostolorum prædicatione in verbo θεοπνευστῳ conscripta? Itaque Patres olim refellebant hæreticos ex verbo Dei: tum subiiciebant Ecclesiam nō aliter docuisse. Vos verò qui falsò ipsam personalem successionē obiicitis,incipite ab Apostolis, vt vestrū Pontificem, vestros Cardinales purpuratos, vestra aulam plusquam regiam, vestra idola, vestrum purgatorium, vestros Monachos, vestros pseudonydonymos clericos, vestram Missam, vestras thearricas & hypocritas ceremonias, vestrum cœlibatum impurum, ex successione doctrinæ in verbo Dei patefactæ demonstretis. Audebi- tisne dicere ipsum exteriorem statum vestrum fuisse Apostolorum temporibus? tantùm abest vt internum splendorem in vera doctrina lucentem retinueritis. Et vt solos vrgeam ponti- ficios Episcopos, omnes à legitimo Successionis ordine iam pridem exciderunt. idq; cum ex præscripto verbi diuini, tum etiam ex ipsorum decretis. Ecquænam est apud vos Pastorum eligendorum ratio? imò est-ne electio? Mittitur pecunia ad Papam, prodit nouus Episcopus nec probatus nec electus. Quid de ipso Papa dicendum, quænam est ipsius electio? imò ex ipsorum decretis à Papa Eugenio sunt ex schismaticis omnes Papæ oriundi. Mirum est Episcopos iam post multa secula imperitos & mutos bene concionantibus successisse. Sic traditioni non successit traditio, siue(vt loquitur Irenæus) præconiationi præconiatio. Non igitur quia alij aliis successerunt: sed qui Apostolicam doctrinam constanter annuntiarūt ij sunt Apostolorum successores dicendi: vt docet Tertullianus & reliqui patres omnes. Quomodo autem diuersitas doctrinæ discernetur? Ex successione Episcoporum, inquis. Minimé: sed si conferatur cum doctrina Apostolica per veros Pastores ex Dei verbo propagata. Prodeant Græci Episcopi, qui successionem suam personalem ostentabunt, disputent vobiscum, quomodo ipsorum errores redarguetis? Nisi verbum Dei opponatis, vnde vera eruetur doctrina Christiana? Quid? monachi nobis obtrudunt Traditiones non scriptas, quia, inquiunt, per manus traditae sunt. Num illas soli Episcopi per manus tradiderunt? Ergo nec doctrina quae verbo Dei innititur quaerenda est in illa Episcoporum successione. Possunt enim doctores esse boni absque illo Episcoporum ordine. Et possumus proferre populos illos qui in Europa semper a pontificiis erroribus abhorruerunt, suosque doctores habuerunt priscam doctrinam Apostolicam docentes.
units.tr: On this succession of persons and bishops, which the Papists boast of, I have written at length in my book on the lawful calling of ministers, and against the monks in the Burdegal. articles 51 and 61; against Turrianus in the Index, article 20; and against his Sophisms in the whole of locus 9 and 10, and in the Repetition of his Sophisms, locus 1, articles 29 to 33 and 46 and 47, locus 9 articles 1, 6 and 7, the whole of locus 10, locus 3 articles 4 and 5, and locus 4 article 9. From these works the refutation of what Arturus here repeats should be sought. At the beginning of chapter 10 of book 3 he seems to pretend that he has not seen Sadeel's writings against Turrianus on this subject, although elsewhere he had said that Turrianus, a most innocent man, is harassed by Sadeel. Sadeel taught in those places, and in the earlier Analysis, that it was easy for the ancients to refute heretics from both successions, since the truth of doctrine was propagated by continuous succession; thus they joined the two successions together. But you, who have fallen away both from the truth of doctrine and from the lawful calling itself, set personal succession against the succession of doctrine, and you value the visible succession of persons above the continuation and perseverance of the apostolic doctrine. Yet the ancients themselves testify that succession of persons counts for nothing if it is separated from the continuation and perseverance of doctrine. For truth can exist without personal succession, and personal succession without truth. This is shown in the Jewish Church. There was also a succession of bishops in the East while Arianism was spreading, but it was not a succession of truth. Is there not a personal succession of bishops in Greece? Why then are they said to have fallen away from the Roman Papists, except that they have abandoned the true doctrine? Therefore succession must be sought from apostolic doctrine. For where does the truth come from? Does it not come from the preaching of the Apostles, written down in the God-breathed word [θεοπνευστῳ]? Thus the Fathers of old refuted heretics from the Word of God, and then they pointed out that the Church had not taught otherwise. But you, who wrongly object personal succession to us, begin from the Apostles, so that you may show from the succession of doctrine revealed in the Word of God your Pope, your purple-clad Cardinals, your court more than royal, your idols, your purgatory, your monks, your pseudo-clerics, your Mass, your theatrical and hypocritical ceremonies, and your impure celibacy. Would you dare to say that your external state was that of the times of the Apostles? So far are you from keeping the inner splendour shining in true doctrine. And to press only the Papist bishops: all of them long ago fell out of the lawful order of succession, and that both by the prescription of the divine Word and by their own decrees. What is the method by which you choose ministers? Or is there even an election? Money is sent to the Pope, and a new bishop appears, neither approved nor elected. What is to be said of the Pope himself, and what is his election? Indeed, by their own decrees all the Popes have descended from schismatics, under Pope Eugenius. It is remarkable that bishops who have been ignorant and dumb for many centuries should have succeeded preachers who spoke well. Thus tradition did not succeed tradition, or (as Irenaeus puts it) proclamation did not succeed proclamation. Therefore those who steadfastly proclaimed the apostolic doctrine are to be called the successors of the Apostles, not those who merely followed one another, as Tertullian and all the other Fathers teach. But how is a difference of doctrine to be discerned? By the succession of bishops, you say. Not at all; but by comparing it with the apostolic doctrine propagated from the Word of God by true ministers. Let the Greek bishops come forward, who will display their personal succession; let them dispute with you. How will you refute their errors, unless you set the Word of God against them? From it alone will the true Christian doctrine be drawn out. What? The monks thrust unwritten traditions upon us, on the ground that they were handed down by hand. Did the bishops alone hand them down? Therefore doctrine which rests on the Word of God is not to be sought in that succession of bishops. For teachers can be good without that order of bishops. And we can point to those peoples in Europe who have always shrunk from Papist errors and have had their own teachers, teaching the ancient apostolic doctrine.

units.la: Quorsum vero obiicitur nobis Episcoporum pontificiorum authoritas, quandoquidem habemus scripta Prophetica & Apostolica? Caeterum statim ab Apostolorum temporibus iam puritatem doctrinae labefactari, & Ecclesiae ordinem declinare coepisse, ipsi Apostoli praemonuerant. Ita igitur de Successione statuendum Apostolica: Eos demum habendos pro Ecclesia Dei qui ex sacris literis suam doctrinam suumque ordinem Ecclesiasticum comprobant. Videmus autem, audimus, legimus pontificios errores quos etiam ex Scriptura reiicimus. Sed iste assertor (ut & reliqui monachi) vult Ecclesiae Romanae dogmata ex Gregorij Rom. pontificis, ex Clementis & aliis eiusmodi scriptis adulterinis (quae tamen ab ipsis pro Traditionibus Apostolicis non scriptis, obtruduntur) afferere: Imo saepius pro Responsione nudas Exclamationes supponit. At inquit iste: Gentibus semper patebit aditus Ecclesia. Ergo Pastores res semper erunt visibiles. Maior illa propositio certa est: sed illi non alligatur assumptio. Nam verbum Dei extat ex cuius perceptione & receptione quae omnibus patet, semper est Gentibus aditus ad Ecclesiam: quamuis non semper sint Pastores boni & fideles qui palam publicè & ex ordine exteriore illud proponant. Hinc intelligitur quomodo in mediis pontificiis tenebris semper fuerint viri pij qui ex sacrorum librorum pia indagatione veram Evangelij doctrinam amplecterentur.
units.tr: But why is the authority of the Papist bishops thrown at us, since we have the prophetic and apostolic writings? Moreover, the Apostles themselves had warned in advance that from the very times of the Apostles the purity of doctrine would begin to totter and the order of the Church to decline. Thus we must lay down the apostolic rule about succession: that those are at last to be regarded as the Church of God who confirm their doctrine and their ecclesiastical order from the holy letters. We see, hear and read the Papist errors, which we also reject from Scripture. But this Assertor (like the other monks) wants to assert the dogmas of the Roman Church from the writings of Gregory, Roman pontiff, from Clement and other such spurious writings, which nevertheless they thrust upon us as unwritten apostolic traditions. Indeed, he often substitutes bare exclamations for an answer. But, says he: The way to the Church will always lie open to the Gentiles. Therefore ministers will always be visible. That major premise is certain, but the minor is not bound to it. For the Word of God exists, and by its perception and reception, which lies open to all, there is always a way to the Church for the Gentiles, although there are not always good and faithful ministers who publicly and openly set it forth in the external order. Hence it is understood how, in the midst of Papist darkness, there were always godly men who embraced the true doctrine of the Gospel through the pious study of the sacred books.

units.la: CAPUT X.
units.tr: CHAPTER X.

units.la: ARturus lib. 3. à cap. 24. vsque ad 33. agit de sua Ecclesiae Nota quinta, quam statuit esse Pastorum ordinationem: eamq; probat ex illo: Quomodo praedicabunt nisi mittantur, Heb. 5. Rom. 10. Item Ephes. 4. dicitur, Dedit, non dabit. Missus est Paulus ab Ecclesia & ordinatus. Item ex Ioan. 10. grex destitutus Episcopis periit. Lutherus autem, Zuingl. Calvinus non fuerunt Episcopi: non igitur potuerunt ordinare: nec habuerint Missionem: sed Sadeelta cuit de Missione, quae pars est vocationis.Haec tractat Arturus vsque ad 28. caput. Capite 28. agit de miraculis quibus ait Protestantes esse destitutos. Quandoquidem Assertor iste argumenta ex Turriano interpolata tantum reponit, non aliis refellendus est rationibus quàm
units.tr: Arturus, book 3, chapters 24 to 33, treats of his fifth mark of the Church, which he holds to be the ordination of ministers. He proves it from "How shall they preach unless they are sent" (Heb. 5; Rom. 10). Likewise Ephesians 4 says, "He gave, not he will give." Paul was sent and ordained by the Church. Also from John 10, a flock deprived of bishops perishes. Luther, Zwingli and Calvin were not bishops, so they could not ordain and had no mission. Sadeel, however, has written on mission, which is a part of calling. Arturus deals with these matters up to chapter 28. In chapter 28 he discusses miracles, of which he says the Protestants are destitute. Since this assertor only reproduces arguments borrowed from Turrianus, he is not to be refuted by any other arguments than

units.la: iis quæ propositæ fuerunt aduersus Turria-num loco scripturæ 9. & 10. & 11. & 12. integris; & ad Repetita ipsius Sophismata, in illis ipsis locis. Item in tractatu de legitima vocatione pastorum.
units.tr: those set out against Turrianus in sections 9, 10, 11 and 12 in full, and by answering his repeated sophisms in those same places. Likewise in the treatise on the lawful calling of ministers.

units.la: Cæterum Apostoli præscripserunt rationem vocationis ordinariæ, stante Ecclesiastico ordine: Hanc rationem observandam esse ita Sadeel affirmauit, vt demonstret Pontificios pastores, Monachos, Pontificem, Cardinales omnino ex ea excidisse. Iam vbi ordo legitimus collapsus fuit, Deus excitauit doctores pios qui puritatem Doctrinæ conseruent, & hoc pertinet ad vocationem quandam extraordinariam: quia recedendum fuit ab illo Pontificum ordine. Recte autem hic contra se Affertor citauit ex Apostolo Siquis Euangelizauerit præterquam quod accepisti, Anathema sit. Item ex Apocal. Siquis apposuerit ad hæc apponet Deus super illu plagas. Nam ex illis quotquot sunt Rom. Pontifices, tot Anathemata constituuntur. Iam si verum est (quod etiam fatetur Arturus) posse Pastores ordinari ex scriptis Apostolicis: certe legitima est illa ordinatio quæ ex illorum præscriptis est instituta. At inquit Affertor. Nisi mittantur quomodo prædicabunt? Respondeo Apostolum ibi loqui de missis à Deo: cuiusmodi fuerant Apostoli extraordinarie missi (nec enim erant ex Leuitis oriundi) At dixit Apostolus, dedit non, dabit: inquit ille, nequis existimet vllos extraordinarios vnquam pastores futuros. Respondit, non excludere, Dabit: sed Dare hic ponere sisignificat, Hebraico more. Sed non dixit Dabit, ne Apostolorum ordinem perpetuò futurum existimes. Locus autem Ioannis 10. aperte Assertoris sententiæ aduersatur. Sic enim ibi. Quotquot ante me venerunt fures sunt, sed non auscultarunt eos oues. Item, qui non ingreditur per ostium, &c. Accommoda hæc tuo Pontifici, & tuis mercenariis Episcopis, & inde colliges quænam sit eorum Missio. Porrò nomine Ordinationis intellige Electionem, & probationem ab Apostolo proponi, quam præcessisse tum constabat, quum manus imponebantur. Superiorem verò Episcopi ordinem præter verbum Dei fuisse institutum, iam aliàs fuit probatum. Atenimuero, quum omnia essent corruptissima, dicimus Pontificios nihil habere quo pluris faciant aliorum Ordinationem quàm Lutheri, Zuinglij, Huss, Wicleffi, Oecolampadij, Farelli, &c. Quòd si illi non fuerunt missi ad prædicandum Euangelium: Ergo eorum qui illos mittebant Missio fuit nulla. Si secus: ergo tum officio functi sunt quum Euangelium pure ex suo munere prædicarunt: & tunc fideliter suum munus exequebantur. Dixisti eorum ordinationem fuisse legitimam, ergo & eorum vocatio. Sed certè tui Papæ & tui Episcopi nunquam mitterent homines ad deregendam suam turpitudinem. Quare Deus ipse misit qui ipsam vocem Dei, vocem Christi, vocem Apostolorum proferrent. Non credes nisi cœlitus ad tuas aures vox illa Dei deferatur? imò non crederes qui toties verbo Dei propositò non credis. Neque nos nouum aliquod fœdus, aut aliquod tertium Testamentum, sed vetus & nouum Testamentum sacrum duntaxat proponimus. Caluinus autem non se intrusit, sed ab aliis pastoribus fuit Ecclesiæ pastor electus: præcessit idonea probatio, consensus Ecclesiæ, & ea quæ in legitima vocatione requiruntur ex Apostolorum præscriptis. Tunc enim iam ordo exterior Ecclesiæ respirare & caput erigere cooperat. Reiciendi sunt quidem quicunque se temere intrudunt: sed nunc agimus de collapso statu & ordine, vbi recedendum fuit ab Episcopis Pontificiis & ipsis Pontificibus, quo veritas doctrinæ & puritas eius retineretur. Cæterum nos sacras & legitimas Ceremonias ex Dei verbo depromimus & pastores eligimus in nostris Ecclesiis ex præscriptis Apostolicis: Arturi & simplium blasphemias & maledicta nihil morati, nō magis quàm istius in Theologia insciitiam qui pag.317. asserit vocationes extraordinarias niti humanis testimoniis. Si centum millia hominum testarentur aliquem missum esse à Deo qui Scripturis repugnaret, illisne credendum esset? Deus (etiam temporibus veteris testamenti) modò adhibuit miracula in extraordinaria missione, modò non: vt patet ex prophetarum missione, de qua aliàs in locis supra citatis. Nostri verò doctores Apostolicam doctrinam illis ipsis Miraculis factis confirmatam in lucem reuocarunt. Si opus Apostolis fuit miraculis veritatem Euangelij de Christo redemptore promulgantibus: Ergo, nunc nobis opus non est miraculis,qui non doctrinam nouam, sed veritatem illam & doctrinam Euangelicam à Pontificiis consepultam in mediū proferimus.Cœrte non proferebantur miracula vt Iudæi crederent Messiam fuisse promissum: sed vt crederet Iesum filium Mariæ Θεάνθρω- πον esse Messiam illum promissum. Non sunt igitur ad hāc doctrinam comprobandam noua miracula quærenda.
units.tr: Moreover, the Apostles prescribed the manner of ordinary calling while the ecclesiastical order stood. Sadeel has affirmed that this manner must be observed, and he shows that the Papist ministers, the monks, the Pope and the cardinals have altogether fallen away from it. Now, where the lawful order has collapsed, God has raised up godly teachers to preserve the purity of doctrine, and this belongs to a certain extraordinary calling, because it was necessary to depart from that order of the Popes. The assertor has also rightly cited against himself the words of the Apostle: "If anyone preaches a gospel other than what you have received, let him be accursed" (Gal. 1). Likewise from the Apocalypse: "If anyone adds to these things, God will add to him the plagues" (Rev. 22). For as many Roman Pontiffs as there are, so many anathemas are established. Now if it is true (as Arturus himself admits) that ministers can be ordained according to the Apostolic writings, then certainly that ordination is lawful which has been instituted according to their prescriptions. But the assertor says, "Unless they are sent, how will they preach?" I reply that the Apostle is speaking there of those sent by God, such as the Apostles were, sent extraordinarily (for they were not descended from the Levites). "But he said, he gave, not he will give," says the assertor, "lest anyone think there will ever be any extraordinary ministers." I answer that "he will give" does not exclude them; rather, "to give" here means "to appoint," in the Hebrew manner. But he did not say "he will give," lest you think the order of the Apostles would be perpetual. The passage of John 10 plainly opposes the assertor's view. For there it reads: "All who came before me are thieves, but the sheep did not listen to them. Likewise, he who does not enter by the door, etc." Apply these words to your Pope and your mercenary bishops, and from them you will gather what their mission is. Furthermore, by ordination understand the election and the testing which the Apostle sets forth, which was known to have preceded the laying on of hands. Moreover, that the superior order of bishops was instituted apart from the word of God has already been proved elsewhere. And yet, since all things were most corrupt, we say that the Papists have no more reason to value the ordination of others than that of Luther, Zwingli, Huss, Wycliffe, Oecolampadius, Farel, and so on. But if those men were not sent to preach the gospel, then the mission of those who sent them was null. If not, then they performed their office when they preached the gospel purely from their duty, and then they faithfully carried out their work. You have said that their ordination was lawful, therefore their calling was too. But surely your popes and your bishops would never send men to correct their own shamefulness. Therefore God himself sent men who would bring forth the very voice of God, the voice of Christ, the voice of the Apostles. Will you not believe unless that voice of God is carried to your ears from heaven? Indeed you would not believe even when the word of God is set before you again and again. Nor do we propose any new covenant or some third Testament, but only the old and new Testament, which are sacred. Calvin, however, did not thrust himself in, but was chosen as pastor of the Church by other ministers: there went before him a fitting testing, the consent of the Church, and the things required for lawful calling according to the Apostolic prescriptions. For then the external order of the Church had already begun to breathe again and raise its head. Indeed, those who rashly thrust themselves in must be rejected; but now we are dealing with a state and order that had collapsed, where it was necessary to depart from the Papist bishops and the Popes themselves, so that the truth of doctrine and its purity might be retained. Moreover, we draw our holy and lawful ceremonies from the word of God, and we choose ministers in our churches according to the Apostolic prescriptions. We pay no heed to the blasphemies and abuse of Arturus and of simple people, any more than to the ignorance of that man in theology who, on page 317, asserts that extraordinary callings rest on human testimonies. If a hundred thousand men were to testify that someone had been sent by God who contradicts the Scriptures, should we believe them? God (even in the times of the Old Testament) sometimes used miracles in an extraordinary mission and sometimes did not, as is clear from the mission of the prophets, which I have treated elsewhere in the passages cited above. Our teachers, however, have brought back into the light the Apostolic doctrine, confirmed by those very miracles that were performed. If the Apostles needed miracles when they proclaimed the truth of the gospel about Christ the Redeemer, then we do not now need miracles, since we are not bringing forth a new doctrine, but that truth and evangelical doctrine which the Papists have buried. Certainly miracles were not displayed so that the Jews would believe that the Messiah had been promised, but so that they would believe that Jesus, the son of Mary, was that promised Messiah [Θεάνθρωπον]. Therefore new miracles are not to be sought to confirm this doctrine.

units.la: Obiicit etiam Assertor cap. 29. eos qui missi sunt extra ordinem non posse in doctrina errare.Lutherum vero fateri se in doctrina ipsa errasse, &c. Respondeo distinguendū esse inter vocationē mediatam & immediatam à Deo factam. Qui mittuntur vocatione mediata, possunt errare, ignorare,labi,alioqui nullus vocatus & missus erraret. Ideo quæ verbo Dei duce ac præuio docent,ea sequimur,quæ secus reiicimus. Nec Lutherum, Caluinum, &c. habemus pro iis Prophetis qui ita fuerint Θεόπνευστοι vt nō debuerint sua scripta exigere ad Scripturam sacram. Nam catenus hominum dogmata sunt recipienda,quatenus ex puris sacræ Scripturæ fontibus genuinè hauriuntur. Nec dicimus Lutherum extraordinariè missum vt Apostoli fuerunt: sed quum esset in ordinaria corruptæ Ecclesiæ Rom.vocatione & missione,Deus illum & similes viros pios excitauit,eísque oculos aperuit, vt in tantis tenebris lucem veritatis ex verbo Dei accenderent. Si in tanta caligine Lutherus titubauit, offendit, impegit, veltræ tenebræ Pontificiæ sunt accusandæ.
units.tr: The assertor also objects, in chapter 29, that "those who are sent outside the ordinary order cannot err in doctrine," and that Luther himself confessed that he had erred in doctrine. I answer that a distinction must be made between a calling mediated and one made immediately by God. Those who are sent by a mediated calling can err, be ignorant, and slip; otherwise no one called and sent would ever err. Therefore we follow what teaches us under the guidance and lead of the word of God, and we reject what teaches otherwise. Nor do we regard Luther, Calvin and others as prophets so inspired by God that their writings ought not be tested by holy Scripture. For human doctrines are to be received only so far as they are genuinely drawn from the pure sources of holy Scripture. Nor do we say that Luther was sent extraordinarily, as the Apostles were; but since he was in the ordinary calling and mission of the corrupt Roman Church, God raised him up and other godly men like him, and opened their eyes, so that in such great darkness they might kindle the light of truth from the word of God. If Luther stumbled, took offence and fell in such great darkness, then your Papist darkness is to be blamed.

units.la: Verùm iste Assertor perinde disputat cap. 29. & 30. vt si Lutherum quasi de cœlo delapsum exciperemus. Agnoscimus opus Dei præstantissimum in Luthero, quòd illum é squalore & sordibus Monachorum excitarit vt fraudes Antichristi detegeret: & sic Deus voluit ipsius & aliorum virorum piorum opera vti, quorum omnium scripta & doctrinam oportet revocare ad sacram Scripturam quam illi normam suæ doctrinæ proponebant.
units.tr: But this Assertor argues in chapters 29 and 30 just as if we had received Luther as one fallen from heaven. We acknowledge that in Luther there is God's most excellent work, in that he raised him from the squalor and filth of the monks to expose the frauds of Antichrist. And so God chose to use his work and that of other pious men, all of whose writings and doctrine ought to be brought back to holy Scripture, which they themselves proposed as the rule of their doctrine.

units.la: Cap.31. multa profert Arturus de Episcopis de quibus fusè in libris supra citatis. Nos autem quum de Episcopis loquimur: de instituto loquimur, non de personis singularibus. Nam plerosque fuisse viros bonos non negamus. Sed ille ordo institutus est, humano consilio ad vitanda schismata. Quid si postea hominum malitia superante, fuerunt in causa corruptæ Ecclesiæ? Libri autem Clementis quos Turrianus & Arturus solent citare, quàm sint infulsi nemo non animadvertit. Multi igitur fuerunt Clementes: qua de re à nostris copiosè disputatum est.
units.tr: In chapter 31 Arturus sets forth many things about bishops, which have been treated at length in the books cited above. When we speak of bishops, however, we speak of the institution, not of individual persons. For we do not deny that most of them were good men. But that order was instituted by human counsel to avoid schisms. What if, later, the malice of men prevailed and they became the cause of a corrupted Church? As for the books of Clement which Turrianus and Arturus are accustomed to cite, anyone can see how spurious they are. There were therefore many Clements; on this matter our people have disputed at length.

units.la: Cæterùm humana instituta quum maximè lædunt, non sunt sequenda: licet ab initio non malis consiliis fuerint propósita. Ex Episcopis ad Archiepiscopos ventum est: ab Archiepiscopis ad Pontificem. Illius humani Institu-ti fibris papatus inuectus nititur. Iudicium presbiterij omissum: Consensus Ecclesiæ neglectus: Electio, probatio legitima relicta: tyrannis, & corruptelæ in Ecclesiam inuectæ.
units.tr: Human institutions, when they do great harm, must not be followed, even if they were proposed at the outset with no bad intention. The bishops gave way to archbishops, and the archbishops to the Pope. The papacy is propped up by the fibres of that human institution. The judgment of the presbytery was set aside, the consent of the Church was neglected, lawful election and testing were abandoned, and tyranny and corruptions were introduced into the Church.

units.la: Cap.32. Arturus asserit Monachorum vocationem
units.tr: Chapter 32. Arturus asserts that the calling of monks

units.la: tionem esse Apostolicam ex Veteribus qui Monachos plurimi fecerunt. At (ut hæc etiam per digressionem dicamus) proles Monachorum qui erant Basilij, Nazianzeni, Chrysostomi, Augustini temporibus, iampridem desiit. Nihil etiam in scriptura de paupertatis voto. sed Monachi fiunt pauperes vt alienis opibus. vescantur. Plerique autem Veteres in istis fuerunt decepti, quum non possent ea prævidere quæ docuit experientia: At tempore Apostolorum nulli erat Monachi, ac nec votum quidem, virginitatis. Sunt, inquit Christus, Enuchi qui se castrarunt: hoc est, qui habent donum continentiæ, quo licet vti absque voto, quibus datum est, inquit, & 1. Cor. 7. Vnusquisque proprium habet donum a Deo. Vos ipsi Monachi vestros Canones & ipsam priscam Monachorum & Clericorum regulam antiquastis, ipsum quoque aerem vestris sordibus inquinastis.
units.tr: ...is apostolic, relying on the Fathers, who made very many monks. But (to say this by way of digression as well) the offspring of the monks who existed in the times of Basil, Gregory of Nazianzus, Chrysostom and Augustine has long since ceased. Nothing in Scripture speaks of a vow of poverty; monks become poor so that they may live on the wealth of others. Many of the Fathers were deceived in these matters, since they could not foresee what experience has taught. But in the time of the Apostles there were no monks, nor indeed any vow of virginity. There are, says Christ, eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs: that is, those who have the gift of continence, which may be used without a vow; to whom it has been given, he says, and 1 Cor. 7: Each one has his own gift from God. You monks yourselves have destroyed your canons and the ancient rule of monks and clergy, and you have polluted even the very air with your filth.

units.la: CAPVT XI.
units.tr: CHAPTER XI.

units.la: Apvt 33. lib. 3. Afferror sextam Ecclesiæ notam dicit esse, Fidei sanctitate, quæ nihilominus Reprobos etiam continet. De hac Ecclesiæ nota satis multa dicta sunt tum in superiori Analysi, tum in aliis tractatibus supra citatis. Illa, inquit Hieronymus, est sancta Ecclesia quæ Christi fidem integram seruat. Hoc autem non facit Ecclesia Rom. Ergo fidei sanctitas non potest esse eius nota. Porrò fidei sanctitas, nec sanctorum communio restringenda est ad professionem Religionis exteriorem. Nam sancti dicuntur propter veram fidem quae est ὑπόκρισις, quę secum habet veram charitatem annexam. Hypocritae sunt igitur qui illam Ecclesiae notam iudicio & opinionibus humanis statuunt.
units.tr: In book 3, chapter 33, he asserts that the sixth mark of the Church is holiness of faith, which nevertheless also contains the reprobate. Enough has been said about this mark of the Church, both in the earlier analysis and in the other treatises cited above. That is the holy Church, says Jerome, which keeps the faith of Christ whole. But the Church of Rome does not do this. Therefore holiness of faith cannot be its mark. Moreover, the holiness of faith and the communion of saints must not be restricted to outward profession of religion. For men are called holy on account of true faith, which is unfeigned [ἀνυπόκριτος] and has true love joined to it. Those therefore are hypocrites who set up that mark of the Church by human judgments and opinions.

units.la: CAPVT XII.
units.tr: CHAPTER XII.

units.la: ASSERTOR Arturus tandē capit. 36. lib. 3. agit de Vnitate quam vult esse septimā & postremam Ecclesię Romanę notam. Ideò prolixè agiit de dissidiis & haeresibus quae natę sunt inter eos qui Reformatam Religionem profitentur. Sed quum illa omnia iam fuerint locis suprà citatis abundè refutata: haec tantùm hîc subiiciemus quae euertunt Arturi vanam hoc loco orationem.
units.tr: Arturus the assertor finally, in chapter 36 of book 3, treats of Unity, which he wants to be the seventh and last mark of the Roman Church. For this reason he has spoken at length about the dissensions and heresies that have arisen among those who profess the Reformed religion. But since all of these have already been sufficiently refuted in the places cited above, we shall add here only those points which overturn Arturus' empty argument on this matter.

units.la: 1. Notae Ecclesiae vocantur hic essentialia ἀδιάφορα a specifica Ecclesiae differentia depromtae, ne semper Arturus in vocabulis Signi & Notae strophas nectat.
units.tr: 1. The marks of the Church are here called essential adiaphora [ἀδιάφορα], drawn from the specific difference of the Church, so that Arturus does not keep stringing together stanzas on the words "sign" and "mark".

units.la: 2. Obiiciunt nobis Pontificij dissensiones & haereses nuper exortas, ad quam obiectionem satis multa iam a nobis suprà dicta sunt. Verùm obsecro, nullae-ne erant dissensiones & haereses Apostolicis temporibus: de hac re legantur Acta Apostolica & Veterum Doctorum scripta. Doctrina verò Ecclesiarum Reformaformatarum non est ex huius vel illius scriptis tantum spectanda, nec ex sermonibus & colloquiis quibusdam: multo minus est ex calumniis & mendaciis monachorum cognoscenda. Fieri autem non potest quin suboriantur difficultates tum circa doctrinam, tum circa voluntatem & animorum coniunctionem. Nonne sunt inter ipsos Pontificios doctores graves controversiae? exempli gratia: Alij volunt Papam esse supra concilium: alij contrà. De Transsubstantiatione quot quantaeque sunt inter illos repugnantes interpretationes? Legantur Formulae Abiurationum Religionis Reformatae, in Gallia vno anno 1585. à Monachis editae & euulgatae, aparebit quàm sint illae inter se diffidentes & contrariae. At vnicam fidei confessionem habent per totam Galliam ij qui Religionem Reformatam sunt amplexi. Quòd si singuli ipsorum Episcopi (quanto magis singuli ipsorum sacrificuli) fidei suae confessionem edere cogerentur in suis dioecesibus: tunc manifestum foret, istos qui nobis dissidia obiectant, inter se maximè dissentire. imò de Christiana doctrina plerosque ne quidem cogitasse. Quòd si ij qui Reformationem expetunt, ab aliis in nonnullis dissideant, danda est opera vt illa placidè componantur: atque id omnino σὺν Θεῷ futurum est: quandoquidem illi in hoc fundamento conueniunt: Ex verbo Dei scripto reformandam esse Ecclesiam & errores pontificios esse ab Ecclesia amouendos. Nondum autem fuit constituta συζήτησις totius Ecclesiae Reformatae consensu. Nec etiam omnes dissensiones circa nonnullos fidei articulos, tollunt Ecclesiam: nec duas Ecclesias contrarias ītatim constituunt.
units.tr: 2. The Papists object to us the dissensions and heresies that have recently arisen, and we have already said a good deal in reply to this objection above. But I ask you, were there no dissensions and heresies in apostolic times? On this matter, let the Acts of the Apostles and the writings of the early Teachers be read. The doctrine of the Reformed Churches is not to be judged from the writings of this or that man alone, nor from certain sermons and conversations, much less is it to be learned from the slanders and lies of the monks. Yet it cannot be that difficulties arise, both concerning doctrine and concerning the will and the union of minds. Are there not serious controversies among the Papist teachers themselves? For example, some want the Pope to be above the council, others the opposite. How many and how great are the conflicting interpretations of Transubstantiation among them? Let the Formulae of Abjuration of the Reformed Religion be read, which the monks published and circulated in France in 1585; it will appear how much they disagree and contradict one another. But those who have embraced the Reformed Religion have one single confession of faith throughout all of France. And if each of their bishops (how much more each of their petty priests) were compelled to publish a confession of faith in his own diocese, it would be plain that these men who object dissensions to us disagree most sharply among themselves, and that most of them have hardly given any thought to Christian doctrine at all. But if those who seek reformation differ from one another on some points, care must be taken that these are settled peacefully; and this will certainly come about with God's help [σὺν Θεῷ], since they agree on this foundation: that the Church is to be reformed according to the written Word of God and that the Papist errors are to be removed from the Church. However, a synod [συζήτησις] of the whole Reformed Church by common consent has not yet been established. Nor do all dissensions concerning some articles of faith destroy the Church, nor do they at once constitute two opposing Churches.

units.la: 3. Veritas ccnfenda est ex veritate. Idem est enim corpus, quia eadem est fides: nec restringitur corpus mysticum ad statum exteriorem certum. Licet sit vna Ecclesia, tamen non semper iisdem ornamentis praefulget: nec semper est doctrina in omnibus eodem modo efficax. Porro fideles locis diuersi, membra sunt eiusdem corporis mystici, licet eundem coetum exteriorem non componant: neque tamen tenemur monstrare, vbinam semper fuerint reliquiae veritatis, de quibus sic olim loquebatur Esaias vt eas non digito monstraret: nec Elias quaerebat vbi locorum esset septem illa millia. Nam Deo constant suae rationes. Satis nobis sit veritatem non posse abolcri aut tenebris extingui. Et cum Chrysostomo affirmamus, ibi Ecclesiam esse, vbi est vera fides. Itaque vnitatem spectamus in doctrina ex sacra Scriptura deprompta: non in successione quadam personarum aut quae ex hominum opinionibus pendeat: & cum Nazianz. statuimus successionem in doctrina litam esse. Augustinus dimufque Athanasium iubentem vt videamus eam quae est ab initio doctrinam, & fidem Catholicae Ecclesiae quam Christus dedit, Apostoli vero praedicauerunt & seruarunt. In hac enim Ecclesia fundamur, & qui inde excidit, Christianus non poterit dici.
units.tr: 3. Truth must be judged by truth. For the body is the same because the faith is the same, and the mystical body is not confined to a fixed external state. Although there is one Church, it does not always shine with the same ornaments, nor is doctrine always equally effective in all. Moreover, the faithful in different places are members of the same mystical body, even though they do not form the same external assembly. Nor are we bound to show where the remnants of the truth have always been, of which Isaiah once spoke in such a way that he did not point to them with a finger, nor did Elijah ask where in the land those seven thousand were. For God's counsels stand firm. It is enough for us that the truth cannot be abolished or extinguished by darkness. And with Chrysostom we affirm that the Church is there where the true faith is. Accordingly, we look for unity in doctrine drawn from holy Scripture, not in some succession of persons or one that depends on human opinions; and with Nazianzen we hold that succession is to be sought in doctrine. Augustine also agrees with Athanasius, who bids us look to the doctrine that is from the beginning, and to the faith of the Catholic Church which Christ gave, which the Apostles preached and preserved. For we are founded upon this Church, and whoever falls away from it cannot be called a Christian.
